mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC posted its largest single-week rebound in the series (-62.1 to -50.3), indicating renewed discretionary outing momentum. This recent acceleration is expected to persist via habit formation, pushing the 4-week mean of RETAIL_REC above the prior 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose 11.8 points week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: If the next four weekly RETAIL_REC means average below -62.1 (the t-1w trough) despite the t-0w rebound, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility crosses above -55 (improving from deeper troughs), it signals renewed public-transport usage that enables more retail and recreation trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the subsequent two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -55 for the week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -62.0 at t-1w to -55.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks following a TRANSIT crossing above -55, or falls instead, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous WORKPLACES recovery and RESIDENTIAL decline indicate people are both leaving home more and resuming office-linked routines, jointly producing a compounding boost to retail-and-recreation visits that exceeds what either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises while RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -56.3 to -47.4 and RESIDENTIAL fell from 18.9 to 15.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise, or rises no more than the sum of single-series effects, when WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL move in these opposite directions together, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility peaked at 46.0 (t-2w) and has since declined to 22.3 (t-0w), consistent with cooling weather reducing outdoor leisure. As outdoor substitutes for retail trips diminish, overall discretionary mobility contracts, lowering RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 20 points from its prior 4-week peak
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 46.0 at t-2w to 22.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks despite a continued decline in PARKS below the 20-point threshold, the seasonal-contraction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility dropped sharply to -56.3 at t-1w then rebounded to -47.4 at t-0w, a pattern consistent with a restriction being tightened and then quickly eased. Such easing typically precedes a broader relaxation of retail and leisure restrictions, raising RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 5 points after a prior week drop exceeding 10 points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -45.3 to -56.3 then rose to -47.4
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase, or continues to decline, within two weeks after such a WORKPLACES rebound pattern, the policy-easing hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has oscillated without a clear sustained uptrend (-10.4, -6.3, -14.1, -8.6), reflecting flat essential-trip demand. Because essential and discretionary trips are correlated through overall household mobility propensity, this flatness signals no compensating rise in discretionary retail, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM shows no sustained directional trend across the four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the next week despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat or declining, the co-movement hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility falling below 16 (from a peak of 18.9 at t-1w to 15.6 at t-0w) indicates reduced home-confinement behavior, consistent with relaxed stay-at-home guidance. This reduced compliance with staying home is expected to translate into more retail and recreation visits over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 18.9 at t-1w to 15.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise, or RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 16 without a corresponding RETAIL_REC increase, the compliance-relaxation hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improved simultaneously at t-0w (TRANSIT from -62.0 to -55.0, WORKPLACES from -56.3 to -47.4), suggesting a joint commuting-recovery regime where more people travel to workplaces via transit, generating incidental retail footfall near transit hubs and office districts, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:Both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved concurrently at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over four weeks following simultaneous TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increases, or rises only in proportion to single-series baseline effects, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.
